title: Bill Coleman leaves and Otis Johnson joins
summary: Russell rarely fired anyone; Coleman probably left for Europe, and Otis Johnson, young and easy to get along with, replaced him beside Red Allen.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Anyway, I want to shortly be playing some more Luis Russell material. At this point, Bill Coleman has left the band. Do you remember any reason why he left?
No, no, unless he went back to Europe. Because he was crazy about Europe. I don't know if he left the band to go back there or not.
But Luis Russell wasn't the kind of bandleader who hired and fired a lot. When he got a man, he....
No, he didn't hire and fire a lot. If a

man was satisfied in the band, he stayed as long as he wanted to. No, Russell was not the type to fire anybody unless he had orders from higher up to fire him. Who was higher up than him? He was the leader.
So chances are, then, that Bill Coleman wanted to leave.

He probably got an offer to go back to Europe, because I know he did go back to Europe, and he stayed over there until World War Two started or something, and he had to come back here. And there was quite a few of the musicians who went to Europe, and they were intent on staying over there. But when the War started they were sent back here. They had to come back. There was quite a few of them.
Now, his replacement apparently is Otis Johnson.
So now you've got Otis Johnson working with Henry Allen, then.
Red was in the band when Otis came in? I can't remember. Yeah, it's possible. Sure.
What do you remember of Otis?
Otis was a nice guy, a nice-looking fellow. He was no trouble. He was very easy to get along with. Good musician. Played his music, and... He hadn't had a
whole lot of musical experience. He was young, as we all were. And he was excited to be in the band, I guess, just like everybody else was. We all got along like brothers and sisters...
